# cuda -- CUDA development toolkit

CUDA compiler, cuDNN, ONNX Runtime, and GPU development libraries. This layer is the **toolkit**,
and it deliberately carries **no driver dependency**: `layer-nvidia` is the *driver*, and the
driver's contract is decided by the substrate, not by the toolkit.

- A **pod** takes the driver from the host: the kernel module is host-global and the runtime
  injects the user-space per container through `/etc/cdi/nvidia.yaml`. A pod image that bakes a
  driver user-space shadows the host's (`layer-cdi`'s `cdi-no-baked-driver-binaries` fails the
  build when it does).
- A **VM** owns its kernel and must bake the driver itself, so a VM / NVIDIA-substrate box
  composes `layer-nvidia` **at the box level**.

A `require:` here is target-blind: it pushed the driver into every pod that composed the toolkit,
and it then had to be stripped again, leaving `layer-nvidia`'s baked `check:` steps asserting
`/usr/bin/nvidia-ctk` on an image whose composition deletes it (opencharly/layer-nvidia#25,
opencharly/spec#395). The toolkit is now installed driver-free at the SOURCE (below), so there is
no strip step at all.

## Packages

PAC: `python-onnxruntime-cpu` in the package arm; `cuda` and `cudnn` are installed by the plan step with `--assume-installed opencl-nvidia` (driver-free — the driver comes from the host through CDI).

**Note:** FFmpeg codec libraries are provided via the `ffmpeg` dependency candy rather than installed directly. CUDA packages come from the standard Arch/CachyOS repos; the Fedora arm was retired with the Fedora CDI boxes (opencharly/distro-fedora#137).

## Arch/CachyOS

The candy is multi-distro. The `distro.arch` section installs `cuda`, `cudnn`,
and `python-onnxruntime-cpu` from the Arch repos. Arch installs CUDA under
`/opt/cuda` — its toolkit headers under `/opt/cuda/targets/x86_64-linux/include/` —
while `CUDA_HOME` is `/usr`, so the Arch path links **every entry of those trees into
`/usr`** — files of any extension and subtrees alike, enumerated rather than
pattern-matched. `nvcc` computes its include root *relative to its own executable*, and
`/usr/bin/nvcc` is a symlink, so anything not reachable under `/usr/include` cannot be
found: `cuda_runtime.h`'s own `#include` fails and every CUDA build dies at CMake's
`enable_language(CUDA)` with "No such file or directory". Matching on patterns produced
both of those failures, on both Arch arms, while every probe in this plan still passed
(opencharly/layer-cuda#9): first a `*.h` glob that linked the top-level headers but not
the `crt/` and `cccl/` subtrees, then the same glob missing the `.hpp` half of the
`_functions` family once the subtrees were linked. The check `cuda-arch-header-root`
preprocesses a real CUDA translation unit to prove the whole header root resolves.

With that stitch in place, the same `nvcc`, header, and library paths resolve
identically on Arch/CachyOS.

## Driver user-space vs the CUDA runtime — installed driver-free at the SOURCE

Installing the toolkit would drag in host-coupled driver user-space: on the pac path `cuda` depends
on `opencl-nvidia` (three driver files), and `cudnn` depends on `cuda`. This layer therefore
installs the toolkit with that dependency treated as satisfied:

```
pacman -Syu --noconfirm --needed --assume-installed opencl-nvidia cuda cudnn
```

The driver reaches a pod from the host through CDI (`podcdi.pod-cdi`), its only provider; the image
bakes none, and there is no strip step any more (opencharly/layer-cuda#39). `layer-cdi` asserts the
result at build time. Measured in a disposable cachyos container: `nvcc` and
`libcudart`/`libcublas` present, zero driver residue, no `nvidia-smi`/`nvidia-ctk`.

The runtime/compute libraries must stay: `libcudart*`, `libcudadevrt*`, `libcublas*`, `libcudnn*`,
`libnvrtc*`, `libcurand*`, `libcufft*`, `libcusparse*`, `libcusolver*`, `libnvJitLink*`. The
anchored predicate (`libcuda.so*`, never `libcuda*`) remains the rule for anyone auditing an image:
the prefix family also spans the runtime (opencharly/layer-cuda#23), and `libcudadebugger.so*` is
driver user-space without the `libcuda.so` stem. The Xorg/NVIDIA-package driver trees are no longer
a subject of this layer — nothing installs them.

## Install tasks

Installs the toolkit driver-free (see above) and stitches `/opt/cuda → /usr` on Arch/CachyOS.

## Usage

A **pod**: compose the toolkit only. The driver is injected by the host through the CDI spec, so
the image names no driver layer at all.

```yaml
# charly.yml — a pod image (CachyOS only; the Fedora CDI boxes were dropped in
# opencharly/distro-fedora#137 — umbrella opencharly/opencharly#1287).
# `pod-cdi` carries the contract and, today, the toolkit; the class split (a wheel-only
# pod composes no toolkit) is opencharly/layer-cuda#39.
comfyui-cdi:
  candy:
    base: podcdi.pod-cdi
    candy:
      - '@github.com/opencharly/pod-comfyui:<tag>'
```

A **VM**: the box names `layer-nvidia` itself, beside the toolkit. The two are siblings at the
box level, never a `require:` inside either layer.

```yaml
# charly.yml — a passthrough-VM box
gpu-vm:
  candy:
    base: cachyos.cachyos
    candy:
      - '@github.com/opencharly/layer-nvidia:v2026.327.0533'
      - '@github.com/opencharly/layer-cuda:v2026.326.2259'
```
